promises.title: A Presidential creative industry advisory team will be established.
promises.promise_blog:
In recent times, Nigeria’s creative industry has garnered global recognition, with its music, film, fashion, and art sectors contributing significantly to the country's economy. As the world shifts towards creative and cultural entrepreneurship, Nigeria stands at a pivotal moment where the potential of the creative industry can be harnessed for national growth and international influence. In light of this, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has made a significant promise to steer the country’s creative sector to greater heights: the establishment of a Presidential Creative Industry Advisory Team. This initiative aims to provide a more conducive environment for the growth of the creative industry and unlock the immense economic potential it holds.

The promise of establishing a Presidential Creative Industry Advisory Team is a timely and strategic move. This team will be tasked with providing expert advice to the government on how to create a more enabling environment for the creative industry. The advisory body will also work on policy recommendations and advocate for reforms that support the creative sector’s growth.
promises.description: A Presidential Creative Industry Advisory Team will be established to steer government efforts in providing a more conducive environment within which our creative industry can flourish.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: we’ll establish a co-operative farmer’s council
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has pledged to establish a Co-operative Farmers' Council as part of his administration's broader strategy to enhance agricultural productivity, ensure food security, and empower rural communities.This initiative aims to provide farmers with a unified platform to access resources, share knowledge, and influence agricultural policies.

While the formal establishment of the Co-operative Farmers' Council is  not forthcoming, the Tinubu administration has already undertaken several measures to strengthen the cooperative movement and support farmers nationwide.
promises.description: We’ll establish a co-operative farmer’s council

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: Establish a presidential fellowship scheme for young nigerians to participate in governance and politics from an early age.
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria faces long-term governance capacity gaps at federal, state and local levels: policy continuity is weak, intergenerational leadership pipelines are thin, and many ministries and agencies struggle to recruit and retain staff with skills in public policy, program delivery, and data-driven management. The dearth of youth with leadership skills have led President Tinubu during his election campaign of 2023 to "Establish a presidential fellowship sheme to give talented and determined young Nigerians new opportunities to experience and participate in governance and politics from an early age." and also to "build on the successes of the one-day Governor program".

These programs if implemented will mentor and build the youth leadership skillsets and creates an institutional pathway to develop high-potential youth into public-sector leaders by offering structured exposure, mentoring, and short-term placements across government.
promises.description: Building on the successes of the one-day Governor Program, we will establish a Presidential Fellowship Scheme to give talented and determined young Nigerians new opportunities to experience and participate in governance and politics from an early age.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: Introduce new social investment programs supporting  Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) particularly among the poor.
promises.promise_blog:
During his Renewed Hope election campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to introduce new social investment programs to foster the growth of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), with a particular focus on supporting economically disadvantaged communities.

This commitment aims to stimulate Nigeria’s economy by creating job opportunities and strengthening the MSME and nano-business landscape, encouraging broader participation and sustainable growth. Recognizing the limited success of previous government efforts to develop MSMEs despite significant resource allocations, the Tinubu administration has introduced targeted programs since its inauguration. These initiatives provide funding, training, and capacity-building support to enhance MSME participation, empower entrepreneurs, and drive economic resilience across the nation.
promises.description: Introduce new social investment programs supporting the development of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) particularly among the poor.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: in the north west and north east, new industrial hubs will focus on textiles.
promises.promise_blog:
The textile industry, once a cornerstone of Nigeria’s economy, is poised for a revival with the establishment of new industrial hubs in the North-West and North-East regions, according to the promise made by President Bola Tinubu. These hubs promise to transform the economic landscape, generate employment, foster innovation, and restore the region’s legacy in textile production.

Historically, Northern Nigeria was a vibrant centre for textile production, supported by an abundance of raw materials like cotton and a skilled workforce. Cities such as Kaduna and Kano were synonymous with textile mills and thriving leather markets. However, years of neglect, competition from imports, and inadequate infrastructure led to the decline of this once-flourishing sector. Major cities like Kano, Kaduna, and Maiduguri are expected to serve as centre points for these hubs.
promises.description: In the North West and North East, new industrial hubs will focus on textiles.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: review the constitutional legislative lists .
promises.promise_blog:
Promise Title: Review the Constitutional legislative lists to ensure that States are given greater control over certain critical matters. Focus areas will include, crime prevention, prisons, stamp duties and certain forms of taxation.

Nigeria’s 1999 Constitution, crafted during military rule, centralises power in a way that often clashes with the realities of governing a diverse, decentralised nation. The Exclusive Legislative List which reserves 68 key areas, including policing, prisons, and taxation, for the federal government—has long stifled subnational innovation. Calls to revise this list, particularly granting states greater control over crime prevention, prisons, stamp duties, and select taxes, are not just bureaucratic tinkering. They represent a critical step toward addressing Nigeria’s most persistent crises: insecurity, economic stagnation, and systemic inequity.

The need for greater resources control has been emphasised over the years as it is one of the pillars of federalism; Nigeria since gaining independence has seen many decisions made from Abuja, most of which are not peculiar to the local settings of respective states, thereby creating frictions.

This promise focused on review of constitutional lists to enable states to take responsibility and take care of these important items. This promise will be tracked by the government efforts in ensuring the removal of legislative restrictions on states to assume these items.
promises.description: Review the Constitutional legislative lists to ensure that States are given greater control over certain critical matters. Focus areas will include, crime prevention, prisons, stamp duties and certain forms of taxation.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: we shall phase out the fuel subsidy.
promises.promise_blog:
An offshoot of the affluent 1970s oil boom era, subsidised fuel prices were seen as a means to improve living standards and stimulate economic growth. But then the 1990s came with unstable oil prices and a plunge in the global oil market, which caused Nigeria to face economic challenges.

To shield the populace from the impact of rising oil prices, successive governments continued and even expanded the fuel subsidy program. By the late 2000s, the cost of fuel subsidies had become a significant burden on the Nigerian government. The government struggled to cover the increasing gap between the international market price of fuel and the subsidised domestic price. This strain on public finances hindered the government's ability to invest in other sectors like education, healthcare, and infrastructure. The subsidy program was plagued by fraudulent practices such as fuel smuggling, subsidy overpayments, and diversion of funds.

These issues led to massive financial leakages and a strain on public finances. According to the World Bank, the Nigerian government spent over $30 billion on subsidy payments in the last 18 years. this promise will be assessed on the government phasing out the subsidy regime completely. In his inauguration speech in May 2023, President Bola Tinubu had announced that “petrol subsidy is gone”.
promises.description: We shall phase out the fuel subsidy.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: Reserve at least three cabinet positions for persons under the age of 40 and 6 more positions for members under the age of 50.
promises.promise_blog:
In his campaign manifesto, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to dedicate at least three cabinet positions to individuals under the age of 40, along with six additional slots for those under 50. The promise underscored his recognition of the potential of young leaders and the value of diverse perspectives in shaping national governance.

At the onset of his administration, this commitment appeared to be taking shape. Three young leaders, Betta Edu (37), Dr. Jamila Ibrahim (37), and Ayodele Olawande (37) were appointed as ministers for Humanitarian Affairs, Youth, and Minister of State for Youth, respectively. Their appointments were seen as a significant step toward fulfilling Tinubu’s vision of greater youth inclusion in government.

However, recent developments have cast a shadow on this progress. Betta Edu was suspended following allegations of financial misconduct, while Dr. Jamila Ibrahim lost her position in the latest cabinet reshuffle. As it stands, Ayodele Olawande remains the only youth representative in the federal cabinet a sharp contrast to the initial promise of broader youth representation.
promises.description: Reserve at least three cabinet positions for persons under the age of 40 and 6 more positions for members under the age of 50.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: institute a pilot student loan regime
promises.promise_blog: This promise will be rated on the creation of a student loan fund and it will be assessed using publicly available official data. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu during his campaign trail for the 2023 general election promised to “We will institute a pilot student loan regime like the program established by the Lagos and Kaduna State Governments” in a bid to open up the tertiary education to more investment and prevent incessant ASUU strikes. This promise, if implemented correctly, will be aimed at revolutionising the students’ tuition financing and making sure students do not defer a session due to inability to pay tuition fee. To make good on his promise, president Tinubu , on Wednesday, April 3, 2024, signed into law the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) (Repeal and Re-enactment) Bill, 2024 an amendment of the 2023 bill aimed at strengthening the Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to carry out its function.
promises.description: We will institute a pilot student loan regime like the program established by the Lagos and Kaduna State Governments

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: our government also shall work with the national assembly to fashion an omnibus jobs and prosperity bill
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria stands at a precipice. With a population exceeding 200 million—over 40% under 25—and an unemployment rate soaring to 4.3% (Q2 2024), the nation’s economic stagnation has morphed into a demographic time bomb. Youth unemployment is even grimmer: 6.5%(Q2 2024) for those aged 15–24, per the National Bureau of Statistics. Add inflation at 31.7%, a currency in free fall, and the crisis becomes existential. In this tinderbox, President Bola Tinubu’s PROMISED to create an Omnibus Jobs and Prosperity Bill.

Nigeria’s history is littered with fragmented, underfunded initiatives: N-Power, YOUWIN, and SURE-P all well-intentioned but hobbled by bureaucracy and corruption. The Tinubu administration aims to break this cycle by consolidating jobs, social welfare, and economic reforms into a single, binding legislative framework. TTo succeed, the Federal Government must collaborate closely with the National Assembly, leveraging constitutional powers (Sections 4, 16) to enact laws promoting economic planning and social justice.
promises.description: Our government also shall work with the National Assembly to fashion an omnibus jobs and prosperity bill

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: promote better inter-agency coordination in foreign policy.
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s promise to establish a Department for Strategic Policy within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs highlights a proactive approach to enhancing Nigeria’s foreign policy apparatus. This reform aims to promote inter-agency coordination, streamline policy formulation, and ensure efficient monitoring and implementation of Nigeria’s diplomatic objectives. By addressing existing gaps in foreign policy management, this initiative can significantly improve Nigeria’s role on the global stage.

As global challenges such as climate change, migration, terrorism, and trade disputes become increasingly interconnected, a more cohesive foreign policy framework is essential to address these multifaceted issues. Nigeria, as one of Africa’s largest economy and a leading voice in regional diplomacy, needs a robust and coordinated foreign policy to maximize its influence in organizations such as the African Union (AU), ECOWAS, and the United Nations. The Department of Strategic Policy, upon its creation, will formulate and implement strategic foreign policies for Nigeria, thereby improving Nigeria's foreign policy standings.
promises.description: Promote better inter-agency coordination in foreign policy. A Department for Strategic Policy shall be established within the Foreign Ministry to improve the formulation, monitoring and implementation of foreign policy.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: full revival of ajaokuta steel company
promises.promise_blog:
Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited (ASCL) popularly known as Ajaokuta Steel Mill is a steel mill in Nigeria, located in Ajaokuta, Kogi State, Nigeria; it is the largest steel mill in Nigeria. The Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited incorporated in 1979, and the steel mill reached 98% completion in 1994, with 40 of the 43 plants at the facility been built. The current administration, in their drive to boost industrial output and increase the contributions of the steel industry to the economy, pledged to the full revival of the ASCL in their 2023 renewed hope Manifesto.

In an effort to resuscitate the plant the previous government of Muhammadu Buhari, signed an agreement with the Russian Export Center to complete and operate the plant but Covid and the Russia-Ukraine war scuttled the plan and the plant remains moribund. The current Minister of Steel Development, Prince Shuaibu Audu, said the FG have reached an advanced stage of raising more than ₦35 billion required to restart the Light Mill Section (LMS) of the Ajaokuta Steel Company. The current update on the government effort to start operation on the Ajaokuta steel plant is still premature to see any positive effects on the plant resuscitation and a lot need to be done for the plant to be operational. This promise is rated “Not started”
promises.description: Full revival of Ajaokuta Steel Company

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: pass legislation promoting female employment in all government offices, ministries, and agencies.
promises.promise_blog:
PROMISE TITLE: Working with the National Assembly, we will aim to pass legislation promoting female employment in all government offices, ministries, and agencies. The goal will be to increase women’s participation in government to at least 35 percent of all governmental positions. This legislation shall also mandate the federal executive (particularly the cabinet and core senior advisers) to reserve a minimum number of senior positions for women. Private institutions shall be strongly encouraged to do likewise.

Inclusive governance is a necessity for a prosperous nation; Nigeria stands at a critical juncture. One of the most promising policy commitments in recent times is the pledge to work with the National Assembly to pass legislation aimed at increasing female employment in all government offices, ministries, and agencies. This initiative, which targets a minimum of 35% female representation across all levels of government, reflects a broader vision for gender equity, national development, and democratic deepening.

For decades, Nigerian women have played pivotal roles in the socio-political and economic fabric of the nation. Yet, their representation in formal government institutions has remained disproportionately low. Despite constituting nearly half of the population, women hold less than 10% of elective and appointive positions at the federal level. This underrepresentation not only undermines democracy but also sidelines diverse perspectives crucial to holistic policymaking.
promises.description: Working with the National Assembly, we will aim to pass legislation promoting female employment in all government offices, ministries, and agencies. The goal will be to increase women’s participation in government to at least 35 percent of all governmental positions. This legislation shall also mandate the federal executive (particularly the cabinet and core senior advisers) to reserve a minimum number of senior positions for women. Private institutions shall be strongly encouraged to do likewise.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: establish an advisory committee to review the existing regulatory environment governing blockchain technology and virtual asset services.
promises.promise_blog:
Promise Title: As part of our reforms, we will establish an advisory committee to review the existing regulatory environment governing blockchain technology and virtual asset services and, where necessary, suggest changes to create a more efficient and business-friendly regulatory framework.

As the adoption of blockchain technology and virtual assets continues to grow, it has become increasingly clear that the existing regulatory landscape requires careful examination. During his campaign for the 2023 general election, the President made the above promise to improve innovation potentially and support the development and regulation of blockchain technology. The advisory committee, as proposed, will play a crucial role in identifying areas where modifications or enhancements to the regulations may be necessary.

Their goal will be to create a more efficient and business-friendly environment that encourages the responsible growth of blockchain and virtual asset services. In the twilight of President Buhari's administration, Professor Isa Pantami, erstwhile minister of communication and the digital economy, inaugurated a National committee on the implementation of the National Blockchain Policy. This committee comprised representatives of all the relevant regulatory agencies; they were saddled with the responsibility of laying out a comprehensive frame work for the implementation of the policy. By taking a comprehensive and strategic approach to regulatory reform, policymakers aim to position the country as a hub for blockchain-based innovation.
promises.description: As part of our reforms, we will establish an advisory committee to review the existing regulatory environment governing blockchain technology and virtual asset services and, where necessary, suggest changes to create a more efficient and business-friendly regulatory framework.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: develop and implement standard curriculum.
promises.promise_blog:
President Tinubu’s pledge to implement a modern, standardised curriculum across all primary and secondary schools in Nigeria is crucial in transforming the country’s education sector.

The benefits of a standardised and modernised curriculum extend far beyond the classroom. By providing a unified foundation of knowledge, this curriculum would ensure that students across the nation, regardless of their location or socioeconomic status, receive a high-quality education. This uniformity would help bridge educational disparities, ensuring that children in underserved areas have the same academic opportunities as those in urban centres.

This promise will be tracked on the government's development and implementation of the new and improved curriculum for primary and secondary schools.
promises.description: A modern standard curriculum will be developed and implemented in all primary and secondary schools throughout the country.

meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: we shall also prioritise the completion of port harcourt – maiduguiri rail
promises.promise_blog:
The eastern rail project is a massive that will link Port Harcourt through Aba, Enugu, Makurdi, Plateau, Bauchi, Yobe and down to Maiduguri the project will be embarked upon by the Federal Government of Nigeria.

The aim of the project is to link the South-South, South-East and North-Eastern part of Nigeria through rail transportation Network, this will improve the socio-economic activities between the regions involved in the project. The project awarded to China Civil Engineering and Construction Company (CCECC) is valued at about $3 billion and measures 1,443 km 1,067 mm narrow gauge rail line.

The project with so much potentials to link the North East, South-South-South and South-East, as of today Nigeria is battling with high food inflation rate, bulk of which is due to the removal of fuel subsidy. Completion of this project will definitely impact the food inflation positively as it will be cheaper to haulage foods from the north through rail than road, this made the president to promise “We shall also prioritise the completion of Port Harcourt – Maiduguiri rail”.
promises.description: We shall also prioritise the completion of Port Harcourt – Maiduguiri rail

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: allocate funds for digitisation of court processes.
promises.promise_blog:
Promise Title: Allocate funds for digitisation of court processes. This will ensure that cases are handled more efficiently by trial courts while also contributing to greater speed and efficiency of the process of appeal

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has pledged to enhance Nigeria's judicial system by increasing the number of federal trial courts and appointing sufficient judges to staff them. This initiative aims to expedite the resolution of disputes and alleviate the burden on the current judicial infrastructure. Additionally, the administration plans to offer administrative and financial incentives to states with congested courts to encourage similar reforms.

Nigeria's judiciary faces significant challenges, including a shortage of judges and an overwhelming backlog of cases. For instance, as of December 2021, the Federal High Court had 75 judges handling approximately 128,000 pending cases, highlighting the immense pressure on the judicial system.
promises.description: Allocate funds for digitisation of court processes. This will ensure that cases are handled more efficiently by trial courts while also contributing to greater speed and efficiency of the process of appeal.

meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: We will embark on the creation of a truly nationwide highway system, connecting all major cities and regions with modern, safe multi-lane highways.
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria, with its vast and diverse landscapes, has always faced challenges in connectivity between major cities and regions; major highways linking regions are old and death-traps to commuters plying the roads, the economic and social exchanges between communities and regions are severely impeded by the lack of good road infrastructure. this great deficit in road infrastructure connectivity made president Tinubu promise to "embark on the creation of a truly nationwide highway system, connecting all major cities and regions with modern, safe multi-lane highways".

The building and completion of the super higghways will definitely improve travel time, security and economic activities within the country as the highway will connect towns, cities, villages together and makes transport of goods and services cheaper, faster and safer.
promises.description: we will embark on the creation of a truly nationwide highway system, connecting all major cities and regions with modern, safe multi-lane highways.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: Enhance Nigeria’s political leadership on the continent by establishing a G-5 among major African nations.
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria is widely referred to as the Giant of Africa since it gained independence for Great Britain in 1960; this is due to the diplomatic role it assumed in Africa geo-political affairs, over the years Nigeria has relinquished such role as it could barely effect its diplomatic positions on erring nations within the ECOWAS. The coups in Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger are examples that Nigeria needs to wake up and assume its role as "Giant of Africa" by making sure it synergize its Africa foreign policy with other big players so as to get things done. The promise by President Tinubu to Enhance Nigeria's leadership on the continent by establishing a G-5 among major African nations is a step in the right direction.

The idea of a G-5 draws inspiration from existing international groupings such as the G-7, G-20, and BRICS, which bring together influential states to coordinate policies, develop common positions, and strengthen their bargaining power on global issues.
promises.description: Enhance Nigeria’s political leadership on the continent by establishing a G-5 among major African nations in order to develop common positions on issues of continental and global importance.

promises.title: Decongest the Apapa port and encourage greater use of other major seaports in the country such as Onne, Warri and Calabar. our policies will include tax relief, credits, relaxed duties and tariffs and other financial incentives.
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has committed to tackling one of Nigeria’s most persistent economic and infrastructural challenges: the congestion at Apapa Port. This initiative aims to "decongest Apapa Port and encourage greater use of underutilized seaports, such as Onne in Rivers State, Warri in Delta State, and Calabar in Cross River State", to revitalize Nigeria’s maritime economy.

The administration’s strategy includes a robust set of policies to alleviate strain on Lagos’s transportation network and enhance the efficiency of Nigeria’s maritime sector. These policies encompass "tax relief, financial credits, relaxed duties and tariffs, and other incentives designed to stimulate activity at alternative seaports". By promoting the use of ports like Onne, Warri, and Calabar, the initiative seeks to distribute maritime traffic more evenly, reduce delays, and foster economic growth across Nigeria’s coastal regions.
promises.description: Decongest the Apapa Port and encourage greater use of other major seaports in the country such as Onne, Warri and Calabar. Our policies will include tax relief, credits, relaxed duties and tariffs and other financial incentives.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: We will establish the media city as a special economic zone.
promises.promise_blog:
In an era where digital content, storytelling, and cultural expression fuel global economies, Nigeria’s creative industry stands as one of its most powerful yet under-leveraged economic assets. From Afrobeats to Nollywood, fashion to animation, Nigerian creatives are breaking boundaries and gaining international recognition. Yet, the infrastructure to support and scale this vibrant sector remains fragmented and underfunded. This made president Tinubu to promise "We will establish the Media City as a Special Economic Zone to attract foreign investment and incentivise both local and international participation in the initiative - Media City modelled on the Dubai Media City. The project will include an international grade conference centre, office park, film studios and sound stages, a university of the arts, auditoriums and performance spaces, exhibition spaces, hotels, and residences."

The infrastructure needed to support, scale, and commercialize the sector remains fragmented, underfunded, and largely informal. Many Nigerian creatives still face structural challenges — limited access to finance, inadequate intellectual property protections, insufficient training institutions, and a lack of purpose-built spaces for collaboration and innovation. These gaps prevent the industry from achieving its full potential as a sustainable driver of economic diversification and job creation.
promises.description: We will establish the Media City as a Special Economic Zone to attract foreign investment and incentivise both local and international participation in the initiative - Media City modelled on the Dubai Media City. The project will include an international grade conference centre, office park, film studios and sound stages, a university of the arts, auditoriums and performance spaces, exhibition spaces, hotels, and residences.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: We shall also prioritise the completion of Lagos - Calabar rail
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to prioritize the completion of the Lagos-Calabar Standard Gauge Rail (SGR) project in his Renewed Hope manifesto, a critical infrastructure initiative aimed at enhancing Nigeria's economic connectivity. This commitment will be evaluated upon the project's completion and its opening for commercial use.

The Lagos-Calabar Coastal SGR is an ambitious infrastructure project designed to connect Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub in the South-West, to Calabar in the South-South. Spanning approximately 10 states, the rail will facilitate the efficient transport of both passengers and freight. Alongside the ongoing Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, this rail project aims to establish shorter, more efficient routes to the South-South and South-East regions from Lagos. These developments are expected to boost trade, reduce travel times for commuters and freight, and unlock significant economic opportunities across Nigeria’s coastal regions.
promises.description: We shall also prioritise the completion of Lagos - Calabar rail

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: A hospitality training program will be established.
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu during the 2023 election campaign for the Renewed Hope mandate has pledged to establish "A hospitality training program aimed at equipping young Nigerians with the knowledge and skills necessary to build a high-quality workforce for the tourism and hospitality industry". This initiative aligns with the administration's broader commitment to youth empowerment and economic diversification through the development of the tourism sector.

Tourism and hospitality remain underdeveloped sectors in Nigeria, despite the country’s rich natural attractions, historical landmarks, and diverse cultural festivals. From the rolling hills of Obudu to the coastal beaches of Lagos, Nigeria holds untapped potential for domestic and international tourism.
promises.description: A hospitality training program will be established to give young Nigerians the knowledge and skills required to create a high-quality workforce for the tourism and hospitality industry.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: A Tinubu government will establish and seed fund an athletes’ welfare fund.
promises.promise_blog:
In his 2023 Renewed Hope manifesto, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to "establish and seed fund an Athletes’ Welfare Fund", a commitment that stirred optimism across Nigeria’s sports community.

This promise is a recognition, long overdue, of the sacrifices and struggles endured by athletes who fly the nation’s flag on global stages but often return to neglect once the applause fades. The proposed Welfare Fund aims to provide financial security, medical insurance, and post-career support for both current and retired athletes critical measures that have long been absent in Nigeria’s sports ecosystem.

For too long, the country has watched its once-celebrated heroes slip into obscurity, many battling illness or poverty, their legacies reduced to fading memories rather than celebrated contributions to national pride.
promises.description: A Tinubu Government will establish and seed fund an Athletes’ Welfare Fund.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: Modernise our ports by deepening the harbour and shipping lanes as well as enlarging berths and docking facilities to allow for the largest cargo vessels to use all Nigerian seaports.
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu during his campaign promised to modernise Nigeria's seaports, aiming to transform them into world-class maritime hubs capable of accommodating the largest cargo vessels.This promise is pivotal for enhancing trade efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and positioning Nigeria as a leading player in West African maritime commerce.

A cornerstone of this modernisation effort is the deepening of harbours and shipping lanes.Currently, Nigerian ports have a draft depth of approximately 12 to 13 metres, limiting their capacity to handle larger vessels.The government's plan is to increase this depth to between 16 and 17 metres, aligning with international standards and enabling the berthing of mega-ships.This enhancement is expected to reverse the trend of cargo diversion to neighbouring ports in countries like Togo and Benin, thereby retaining significant revenue within Nigeria's economy.

In tandem with deepening efforts, the administration is focusing on enlarging berths and docking facilities across all Nigerian seaports.This expansion will facilitate the accommodation of larger vessels and increase the throughput capacity of the ports.The Federal Executive Council has approved contracts for the modernisation of the Western Ports, including the Lagos Port Complex and Tin-Can Island Port Complex.These upgrades are projected to generate over 20,000 jobs and stimulate economic activities in the maritime sector.
promises.description: Modernise our ports by deepening the harbour and shipping lanes as well as enlarging berths and docking facilities to allow for the largest cargo vessels to use all Nigerian seaports.

This initiative aims to equip young Nigerian entrepreneurs with essential skills in managerial knowledge, financial management, and organizational structure, offering them a competitive edge on the global stage.

Furthermore, the Digital MSME Academy could stimulate economic growth and job creation. With great number of Nigerian youths  operating MSMEs business in Nigeria, strengthening their capabilities could lead to more robust economic activity and generate employment opportunities, helping to alleviate the nation’s high unemployment rate. By fostering a culture of continuous learning, the academy could also drive innovation, inspiring entrepreneurs to develop new solutions tailored to Nigeria’s unique needs.
promises.description: We will establish a digital MSME Academy to provide continuous learning opportunities for young entrepreneurs, giving them access to experts and advice on global best practices in order to improve their business development through increasing managerial know- how, financial management and organisational structure.

promises.title: End incessant Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) strike
promises.promise_blog:
For decades, the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) has been at the center of Nigeria’s higher education debates, representing the collective voice of university lecturers and academic staff. Its frequent strikes, though often frustrating for students and parents, highlight the deep-rooted challenges in the sector underfunded universities, crumbling infrastructure, poor welfare for lecturers, and broken promises from government agreements. These repeated disruptions have stalled academic calendars, delayed graduations, and cast uncertainty over the future of countless young Nigerians.

It is against this backdrop that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to put an end to the cycle of incessant ASUU strikes. His promise carries the weight of hope for millions who dream of a stable and reliable education system. By addressing funding gaps, improving staff welfare, and fostering genuine dialogue with ASUU, this commitment has the potential to restore confidence in Nigeria’s universities and safeguard the academic future of the nation’s youth.
promises.description: End Incessant Asuu Strike

promises.title: Ensure that investors and foreign businesses repatriate their hard-earned dividends and profits home
promises.promise_blog:
In today’s competitive global economy, the ability of foreign investors to repatriate their earnings freely is vital for attracting and sustaining investment. During the 2023 campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to ensure that "investors and foreign businesses repatriate their hard-earned dividends and profits home". If implemented, this commitment would not only enhance investor confidence but also position Nigeria as a stable, reliable, and business-friendly environment capable of driving economic growth and global competitiveness.

This, in turn, can stimulate greater foreign direct investment (FDI), which has long been touted as a key driver of technological transfer, job creation, and broader economic transformation in developing countries.
promises.description: We shall ensure that investors and foreign businesses repatriate their hard-earned dividends and profits home

promises.title: the great green wall of the north will be fully completed.
promises.promise_blog:
Stretching across the width of Africa, the Pan-African Great Green Wall (GGW) stands as one of the continent’s most ambitious environmental and socio-economic undertakings. Conceived in 2007 by the African Union, this massive initiative aims to combat desertification, restore degraded land, and create sustainable livelihoods across the Sahel region, an area rapidly losing arable land to the encroaching Sahara desert. As one of the key member states, Nigeria has played a significant role in realising this vision, especially through the establishment of the National Agency for the Great Green Wall (NAGGW) in 2015.

Over the years, Nigeria’s efforts have evolved from modest afforestation campaigns into a national strategy linking land restoration with poverty alleviation, food security, and conflict prevention. Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration, the project gained renewed momentum. With a sharpened focus on climate resilience, green jobs, and community-led agroforestry, Nigeria has made significant strides in shelterbelt expansion, seedling distribution, and cross-sector partnerships.
promises.description: The Great Green Wall of the North will be fully completed.

promises.promise_blog:
Before modern roads and railways, Nigeria’s rivers and canals especially the Niger and Benue were vital routes for trade, travel, and communication. During his campaign for the 2023 general election, President Tinubu pledged to Embark on a dredging campaign for our most strategically important inland waterways to make and keep them navigable for the passage of goods and people to keep these key inland waterways navigable for the movement of goods and people.

Dredging Nigeria's waterways will reduce stress on Nigeria’s highways which suffer from chronic congestion and overuse, leading to high maintenance costs and frequent accidents. Shifting freight to waterways would ease the burden on roads, reduce wear and tear, lower logistics costs, and cut carbon emissions.
promises.description: Embark on a dredging campaign for our most strategically important inland waterways to make and keep them navigable for the passage of goods and people.

promises.title: Support the allocation of about 1% of pooled health insurance funds to health research.
promises.promise_blog:
During his campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu emphasised the critical role of health research in shaping a resilient and responsive healthcare system. Among his notable promises was the commitment that "Our government will support the allocation of about 1% of pooled health insurance funds to health research, through research grants and support for institutions involved in health research." This seemingly technical policy proposition carries deep implications for Nigeria’s health sector and its future preparedness for both routine and emergency healthcare needs.

Health research is the backbone of evidence-based policymaking, enabling governments to craft interventions that are not only timely but tailored to the specific health realities of their populations. In Nigeria, a country facing a broad spectrum of health challenges such as maternal mortality,  infectious diseases like malaria and Lassa fever to rising non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and cancer, research is essential to uncovering effective, localised, and sustainable solutions.
promises.description: Our government will support the allocation of about 1% of pooled health insurance funds to health research, through research grants and support for institutions involved in health research.

This practice has stifled business growth, discouraged investment, and contributed to the rising cost of goods and services. Recognizing these challenges, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to address all complaints related to multiple taxation and ensure the system is harmonized. The goal is to create a more business-friendly environment, reduce unnecessary tax burdens, and enhance the efficiency of revenue collection.

The promise will be evaluated based on the government’s establishment of a tax review committee mandated to assess complaints on multiple taxation and provide actionable recommendations for harmonization.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: our healthcare delivery strategy will target poor and marginalised communities.
promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's promise to reform Nigeria’s healthcare system emphasises inclusivity by stating during his campaign trail for the 2023 general election that "Our healthcare delivery strategy will target poor and marginalised communities, leaving nobody behind." he further emphasised that he will "expand service delivery to marginalised groups through the use of demand-side incentives and the establishment of a regulated community-based health insurance scheme within the broader National Health Insurance Scheme"", aiming to ensure no one is left behind, particularly poor and marginalised communities.

 Launched in 2005, Nigeria’s National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) aimed to be a lifeline. On paper, it’s elegant: formal sector workers contribute 5% of their salary, employers add 10%, and coverage includes everything from malaria treatment to surgeries. But 19 years later, only 9% of Nigerians are enrolled mostly federal employees and corporate workers. The informal sector? over 90% of the population, from street hawkers to artisans, remain in the cold, relying on prayer, herbal remedies, or predatory loan sharks when illness strikes. Corruption, infrastructure gaps, and a distrust of bureaucracy have turned universal health insurance coverage into a ghost promise for many.

The 2022 National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) Act declared health insurance mandatory for all citizens and established a fund for vulnerable groups. When the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) Act was signed into law in May 2022, it was hailed as a watershed moment for Nigeria’s healthcare system. For the first time, health insurance was declared mandatory for every Nigerian, with provisions to cover vulnerable populations and expand access to care. One of the NHIA Act’s most celebrated provisions was the Vulnerable Group Fund (VGF), designed to provide free health insurance for low-income Nigerians, including pregnant women, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities.The Act promised to bridge the gap between the privileged few with insurance and the millions left to fend for themselves.
promises.description: Our healthcare delivery strategy will target poor and marginalised communities, leaving nobody behind. We will expand service delivery to marginalised groups through the use of demand-side incentives and the establishment of a regulated community-based health insurance scheme within the broader National Health Insurance Scheme.

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: rehabilitation of the lake chad basin ecosystem and other subnational economic systems affected by violent groups.
promises.promise_blog:
During his 2023 presidential campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to rehabilitate the Lake Chad Basin ecosystem and revive subnational economic systems devastated by violent groups. This commitment was framed not only as an environmental project but also as a pathway to regional stability, poverty reduction, and long-term security. The promise directly responds to decades of environmental decline and the economic collapse of communities in one of Nigeria’s most fragile regions.

The Lake Chad Basin, shared by Nigeria, Chad, Niger, and Cameroon, was once a thriving ecosystem supporting agriculture, fishing, and pastoralism for over 30 million people. In the 1960s, the lake covered more than 25,000 square kilometers. Today, due to climate change, desertification, and unsustainable water use, its surface area has shrunk by about 90 percent. This ecological disaster has crippled livelihoods and fueled competition over scarce resources, often escalating into conflict.

The decline of Lake Chad coincided with the rise of violent insurgent groups such as Boko Haram and ISWAP, who exploited local grievances and the collapse of traditional economic systems. Fishing communities lost their harvests, farmers abandoned dried lands, and pastoralists were pushed into conflict over dwindling grazing areas. The humanitarian consequences have been severe, millions displaced, widespread hunger, and entire local economies disrupted.
promises.description: Rehabilitation of the Lake Chad Basin ecosystem and other subnational economic systems affected by violent groups.

promises.title: the tax regime applicable to the creative sector will be revised.
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria’s creative sector is a cultural goldmine and an economic powerhouse in waiting. From the global appeal of Afrobeats to Nollywood’s global storytelling, Nigerian creatives are redefining the nation’s global image. Yet, the policies that govern this sector remain outdated, fragmented, or ill-suited to the realities of creative work. Nowhere is this more evident than in Nigeria’s tax regime.

In 2023, the Nigerian government passed the Finance Act and other tax-related reforms aimed at expanding the tax net and boosting revenue. While these moves are essential for economic stability, they risk stifling one of the country's most dynamic sectors if not adapted to its unique structure. Most creatives operate as freelancers, gig workers, or micro-enterprises often without the financial literacy, accounting systems, or legal support that formal tax compliance demands.
promises.description: The tax regime applicable to the creative sector will be revised to better incentivise local production and attract foreign producers to Nigeria.

promises.title: sokoto - eliminating kidnapping
promises.promise_blog: In recent years, kidnapping and its adjacent vices have become lucrative activities in the country. Though Nigeria's security situation has been a concern for decades, over the past 15 years, occurrences of kidnapping have grown exponentially, and successive governments have pumped trillions of naira annually into the defence budget aimed at eliminating insurgency and kidnapping in the country. Seeing how existential this crisis was, president Tinubu promised to wipe out kidnapping in his renewed hope manifesto. The effects of this nefarious act are felt all over and have affected the economic activities of the country, preventing communities from engaging in their means of livelihood, increasing the number of unemployed citizens and affecting their quality of life. Since 2019, Nigeria has experienced 735 mass abductions, according to the consultancy firm SBM Intelligence. The firm reported that between July 2022 and June 2023, 3,620 people were abducted in 582 kidnapping incidents, with approximately 5 billion naira ($3,878,390) paid in ransoms. In another report by the BBC, over 3600 people were kidnapped in the country within a year, "the most ever" recorded, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data figures. These include kidnapping of school children, farmers, and internally displaced. This kidnappings are most rife in the northern and middle-belt region, the source of most of the country's farm produce; this affects the food supply chain and increases the chances of a food famine happening.
promises.description: Sokoto - Eliminating kidnapping

promises.promise_blog:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, during his campaign, made a promise that "Inaugurate a Youth Advisory Council to the Employment Action Plan which we will develop". A platform designed to give young people a voice in shaping policies that directly affect their lives. This wasn’t just another political promise; it felt like a genuine attempt to bridge the gap between the government and the youth, who often feel left out of critical decision-making processes. The idea was simple yet powerful: let the youth have a seat at the table, let them contribute their ideas, energy, and perspectives to help craft an Employment Action Plan that addresses one of the most pressing issues in the country—youth unemployment.

Now, let’s break this down a bit. Youth unemployment in Nigeria isn’t just a statistic; it’s a lived reality for millions of young people. It’s the graduate who has been sending out CVs for years with no callbacks. It’s the skilled artisan who can’t find steady work. It’s the young entrepreneur with big ideas but no access to funding or mentorship. It’s a problem that keeps many awake at night, not just because of the financial strain but because of the emotional toll it takes.

This promise will be tracked based on efforts taken by the government to inaugurate a youth council.
promises.description: Youth Advisory Council: Inaugurate a Youth Advisory Council to the Employment Action Plan which we will develop.

promises.promise_blog: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, during his campaign trail, promised to “End Estimated Electricity Billing”. This is aimed at ending random billing of customers by the Distribution companies (DISCOs), this practice have been a burden on electricity consumers over the years as unmetered ones are billed disproportionately from the number of electricity units they used. According to the NERC 2023 second quarter report, as of June 30, 2023, there are 12,561,049 registered electricity customers with 44.16 per cent (5,546,483) of them metered leaving 55.84 per cent (7,014,566) of customers unmetered. The NERC report on metering shows that there are more than half of electricity consumers in Nigeria without meter to record and bill their electricity usage accordingly.
promises.description: End Estimated Electricity Billing

meter.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu
meter.description: This meter monitors the promises of the President of Nigeria, His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu

promises.title: Enhance aircraft safety, improve incident reporting, ensure fair ticket pricing, and provide compensation for flight delays or cancellations
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria’s aviation sector plays a vital role in connecting people, businesses, and markets across the country and beyond. With millions of passengers flying each year, the sector is not only central to mobility but also contributes significantly to trade, tourism, and economic development. However, despite its importance, Nigeria’s aviation industry has long been plagued by systemic challenges that undermine efficiency, safety, and consumer trust. The president, Bola Ahmed Tinubu promised in his 2023 election campaign to "improve aircraft maintenance, safety measures and incident reporting requirements regarding domestic airlines and ensure fairness and transparency in ticket pricing for both international and domestic airlines." and to also "includes providing compensation to passengers for significant flight delays or cancellations attributable to the conduct of the airline or its staff."  

One of the most pressing issues has been aircraft maintenance and safety compliance. Many domestic airlines struggle with high operating costs, foreign exchange constraints, and limited access to modern maintenance facilities. As a result, aircraft are often serviced abroad, increasing expenses and turnaround times. While Nigeria maintains safety oversight through the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), past incidents and near misses highlight the need for stricter, transparent, and more proactive safety enforcement. Strengthening maintenance protocols and ensuring timely incident reporting will not only improve safety but also align Nigeria’s aviation industry with international standards set by bodies such as the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

Another major concern is ticket pricing and consumer protection. Nigerian passengers often face unpredictable and inflated fares on both domestic and international routes. Pricing practices lack transparency, with surcharges and fluctuating rates eroding consumer confidence. The absence of robust compensation frameworks has further disadvantaged passengers who experience significant delays or cancellations. While some airlines cite operational challenges — including fuel scarcity, poor airport infrastructure, and volatile exchange rates — passengers are left bearing the brunt of inefficiencies beyond their control.
promises.description: We shall improve aircraft maintenance, safety measures and incident reporting requirements regarding domestic airlines and ensure fairness and transparency in ticket pricing for both international and domestic airlines. This includes providing compensation to passengers for significant flight delays or cancellations attributable to the conduct of the airline or its staff.

promises.promise_blog:
For years, the former administration of President Muhammadu Buhari  touted the idea of Air Nigeria bringing back the glory day of the national carrier but it did not materialise until the tail end of the administration the aviation ministry unveiled Nigeria Air, which was cancelled by the current administration which promised to fulfil the promise of seeing Nigeria Air in the sky.
This strategic move represents a significant milestone in the nation's aviation history. The creation of a national airline is poised to bring a host of benefits, from enhancing connectivity and boosting tourism to fostering economic growth and strengthening the country's global competitiveness.


In 2023, the Ministry of Aviation, under Hadi Sirika, former minister, unveiled Nigeria Air three days before the end of former President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration. 
The development had elicited concerns among stakeholders nationwide over the ownership arrangement, which gave Ethiopian Airlines a 49 per cent equity stake.  The Federal Government had 5 per cent equity, while a consortium of three Nigerian investors had 46 per cent. 
Reacting to the deal in June 2023, the House of Representatives asked the Federal Government to suspend the operations of Nigeria Air, describing it as a fraud.

The situation has been particularly dire in rural areas, where access to electricity remains a significant challenge. This great challenge to the power situation of the country made President Bola Tinubu promise “Electricity will become more accessible and affordable to businesses and homes alike.” Contrary to the promise of accessibility and affordability of electricity promised by the president, the government has embarked on a policy of discrimination by reinforcing the band system of electricity supply and increasing tariffs for the privileged band, this move contradicts the promise of the president to make electricity more accessible and affordable to businesses and households and the electricity, However, on a year-on-year basis, electricity supply decreased by 1.41% compared to 5,851.87 (Gwh) reported in Q1 2023.

promises.title: food shall be made more abundant yet less costly
promises.promise_blog:
Access to affordable food is a fundamental human need and a critical component of economic and social stability. When food prices are high, it places a significant financial burden on households, forcing difficult trade-offs between food and other necessities like housing, healthcare, and education. Conversely, lower food prices can have far-reaching benefits for individuals, families, communities, and the nation at large.

In July 2023, the President declared a state of emergency to curtail food shortages and rising food prices; all matters concerning essential food and water were moved under the purview of the National Security Council, which comprises the country's security chiefs and is led by the president.

The importance of low food prices can be seen through several key lenses. From an economic standpoint, affordable food allows consumers to stretch their budgets further, leaving more discretionary income to spend on other goods and services. This boosts overall consumer demand and fuels economic growth. For low-income households in particular, lower food costs can be the difference between making ends meet or falling into poverty.
promises.description: Food shall be made more abundant yet less costly

promises.title: improve and maintain airport runways and other aviation infrastructure.
promises.promise_blog:
Promise Title: We will establish and enforce a policy for the timely and adequate maintenance and improvement of airport runways and other critical aviation infrastructure.

Nigeria’s aviation sector sits at a critical juncture, plagued by decades of neglect, underinvestment, and structural decay, especially the maintenance and modernization of airport runways and related infrastructure. Despite being one of West Africa’s major aviation hubs, Nigeria has long grappled with outdated runways, insufficient maintenance regimes, and safety issues that compromise passenger experience and operational efficiency.

At the heart of Nigeria’s aviation woes is a fundamental issue: many of the runways in use today were constructed in the 1970s and 1980s, with a standard lifespan of 20 to 25 years. That lifespan has long expired, and the consequences are showing. Cracked surfaces, eroded shoulders, inadequate lighting systems, and poor drainage plague multiple airports, resulting in flight delays, temporary closures, and compromised safety standards.
promises.description: We will establish and enforce a policy for the timely and adequate maintenance and improvement of airport runways and other critical aviation infrastructure.

promises.title: we shall make permanent a biannual “state of the youth” survey to create a platform for young nigerians to give feedback to government.
promises.promise_blog:
Nigeria is a country with a massive youth population; over 70% of its people are under the age of 30. These young people are the backbone of the nation, the drivers of innovation, creativity, and economic growth. Yet, for far too long, their voices have been sidelined in decision-making processes. Policies are often designed without their input, and programs meant to empower them frequently miss the mark because they don’t address the real challenges young people face. The “State of the Youth” survey is a way to change that. It’s a way to say, “Your opinion matters. Your experiences matter. And we need to hear from you to get this right.”

The biannual nature of the survey is particularly significant. It’s not a one-off thing; it’s a consistent, ongoing effort to check in with young Nigerians and gauge how they feel about the government’s performance. This regularity ensures that youth issues remain a priority on the national agenda.

This promise will be assessed based on the government's efforts to get feedback from youth across the country.
promises.description: We shall make permanent a biannual “State of the Youth” survey to create a platform for young Nigerians to give feedback to government regarding their opinions on the performance of government, paying special attention to youth empowerment programs and policies.
